mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more, coinciding with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) of less than 0.5%, indicates a supply-side contraction with weak housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% and HOUST rises <0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: manufacturing slowdown with weak housing demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO drops >1% and HOUST increases <0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk aversion and reduces equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of at least 0.5% over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS increases >0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration from negative to positive, with a magnitude above 0.3%, signals labor market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS changes turn from negative to positive and exceed +0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS turns positive and exceeds +0.3% after a negative reading.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based expansion in economic activity, which raises earnings growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise >1% in the same month.
